newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-German shares power ahead to new records.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German shares power ahead to new records.

text.p: German shares powered ahead to new highs on Thursday, confounding expectations that the market would take a breather after its big surge last week.
"The rally is feeding the rally," said one trader. Frankfurt's bull run has been helped by the strengthening dollar which has boosted prospects for German exporters.

The DAX index of Germany's leading 30 shares ended floor trade at a record closing high of 2,909.91 points, up 43.84 points, or 1.53 percent. It had been even higher, reaching a peak of 2,914.61 earlier in the session.
"The fact that the dollar has stabilised at its new highs has been encouraging," said one trader.
The dollar reached up to 23-month highs on Tuesday above 1.57 marks and then stabilised around 1.56 marks, boosting shares in German exporting stocks in particular.

But the dependence of the German market on the strength of the dollar was shown in post-bourse electronic dealings when the IBIS DAX slipped off record highs to trade under 2,900 points as the dollar lost ground.
Dealers added that German data showing a higher-than-expected climb in unemployment, which eased inflation worries, had also been supportive for the market.
German unemployment rose 50,000 to another post-unification record of 4.1 million on a seasonally adjusted basis in November.
Dealers said year-end buying by German institutional investors, some of whom have been left behind in the speed of the current climb, was adding to the bullish frenzy.
The DAX index has ended bourse trading at seven record highs in the last nine trading days, soaring a total of 146 points, or 5.3 percent.

"Many players are surprised that the market has risen so fast," said one trader, "But the rally is not over yet. We're still in a bullish phase and there's still potential in many stocks. The DAX could make 3,000 points by the year end."

The DAX has been powered on in the last two weeks by a combination of a firmer dollar and German government bond strength, sparked by fresh speculation that German interest rates may still have room to fall.
During Thursday's trade, the DAX held onto most of its gains, despite the Bundesbank announcing that it had not lowered key interest rates, pushing Bunds lower.

Last week the bourse soared through analysts' old year-end target of 2,850, forcing many to revise their forecasts upwards to 2,900 for the end of the year and even the once unthinkable 3,000 point mark for the medium term.
The DAX index has gained over 650 points, or almost 30 percent, since the beginning of the year, but in the last couple of months the rally has accelerated even faster.

The recent surge was sparked last week when the dollar came off lows around 1.50 marks as France and Germany made comments suggesting they favoured a stronger dollar against both the mark and the Franch franc, rekindling speculation that Germany could again lower interest rates.
But some analysts warned that euphoria had caused the market to lose sight of economic fundamentals.

"The current high level of the DAX prices in a lot of optimism and is only justified when interest rates continue to fall and company results are very good next year," said Commerzbank analyst Peter Pietsch.
Some traders agreed, saying the market was very overheated at the moment and would benefit from a pause before advancing further.
"I must warn that we cannot continue to climb without some consolidation. And that's what many investors are praying for because they have been left behind in the rally," said one dealer.
